Coati 0.2.1-alpha makes the results document say more of what a solved model says, in the same terms for Calliope, PyPSA and AdOpT-NET0: the energy each store holds at each time, the marginal price of each carrier at each location, the cost told into what is paid for having the capacity and what is paid for operating it, the emissions of each technology, and what a generator could have put out from its resource but did not. Coati is a Python package and command line tool that read the netCDF and HDF5 result files of the three frameworks and write them as JSON; it needs none of the frameworks, nor xarray: h5py and NumPy suffice.

It is an alpha. The layout of the document moves to `schema_version` 1.1: new keys, all of them optional, and nothing that a reader of 1.0 relies on has changed; the schema of 1.0 stays published next to that of 1.1. The Python interface and the command line may still change between pre-releases. If a document says something other than what a framework says about the same file, please [open an issue](https://github.com/enerplanet/Coati/issues) with the file and the two numbers.

## Highlights

- **Storage levels.** `storage_levels` holds the energy of each store at each time: the state of charge of a PyPSA storage unit and the energy of a store, `storage` of Calliope, `storage_level` of AdOpT-NET0.
- **Prices.** `prices` holds the marginal price of each carrier at each location at each time, what one more unit would cost, as the framework reports it: the marginal price of every bus of PyPSA, and the shadow price of the balance of Calliope 0.7 where a model asks for it.
- **Costs told apart.** `fixed_costs_by_location` is what is paid for having the capacity, the annualised investment and the fixed costs of operation; `variable_costs_by_location` what is paid for operating, fuel and the variable costs of operation, imports less exports. Every entry of `costs_by_location` is the sum of its two parts.
- **Emissions.** `emissions_by_location` and `total_emissions`, as each framework records them: PyPSA by what is burnt times what the carrier emits, as PyPSA counts it towards a cap; Calliope by the class of cost named `emissions`; AdOpT-NET0 by what each technology emits less what it takes up. PyPSA's caps are reported under `details.global_constraints` with their shadow prices.
- **Curtailment.** `curtailment` is what a generator whose availability varies with time, the sun or the wind, could have put out but did not.
- **The figures of Calliope.** The cost of every class as the file has it, the systemwide capacity factors and levelised costs, the total levelised cost, the total generation, the use of the sources and the supply that was not used, under `details`.
- **Checked against the frameworks.** Every new key was compared with what the framework itself reports, for the files under `tests/data`, whose facts were written anew with PyPSA 0.25.2, 0.35.2, 1.2.4 and 1.3.0, Calliope 0.6.8, 0.6.10, 0.7.0.dev7 and 0.7.0 and AdOpT-NET0 0.1.10, and for all 197 result files of the scenarios and examples of [MEME](https://github.com/enerplanet/meme) 0.2.0-alpha.

| Identifier | Framework | Versions | Tested with | Formats |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `calliope-v0-6` | Calliope | 0.6.x | 0.6.8, 0.6.10 | netCDF-4 |
| `calliope-v0-7` | Calliope | 0.7.x | 0.7.0.dev7, 0.7.0 | netCDF-4 |
| `pypsa-v0` | PyPSA | 0.25 and later 0.x | 0.25.2, 0.35.2 | netCDF-4, HDF5 |
| `pypsa-v1` | PyPSA | 1.x | 1.2.4, 1.3.0 | netCDF-4, HDF5 |
| `adopt-net0-v0-1` | AdOpT-NET0 | 0.1.x | 0.1.10 | HDF5 |

## Getting it

```bash
pip install enerplanet-coati               # once the package is on PyPI
pip install enerplanet_coati-0.2.1a0-py3-none-any.whl   # the wheel attached below
coati results.nc results.json calliope-v0-7-0
```

Python 3.10 or newer. The package is called `enerplanet-coati` on PyPI, the Python package and the command `coati`; `0.2.1a0` is how Python writes the version `0.2.1-alpha`.

Documentation: <https://enerplanet.github.io/Coati> (quickstart, command line, Python package, how each key follows from a file of each framework, the documents and their schemas, reading the bundles of MEME).

## What changed

The full list is in the [changelog](https://github.com/enerplanet/Coati/blob/v0.2.1-alpha/CHANGELOG.md#021-alpha---2026-10-25).

## Known limitations

- Prices are read where a file holds them: PyPSA writes them for every bus; Calliope 0.7 writes the shadow price of its balance only if the model asks for it, and not with the CBC solver; AdOpT-NET0 writes none.
- Emissions follow the conventions of each framework: PyPSA's caps are read from `carriers.co2_emissions`, Calliope's from a class of cost named `emissions`, and the emissions of what AdOpT-NET0 imports and of its networks are in `details.summary` alone.
- Curtailment is counted for PyPSA generators whose `p_max_pu` varies with time, which is what records a resource; the spare capacity of a dispatchable plant, which `n.statistics.curtailment` of PyPSA 1.2 also counts, is not curtailment to the document. Calliope and AdOpT-NET0 record no availability the document could use.
- The two parts of the cost are present where the file tells them apart; the operate mode of Calliope 0.7 writes them not.
- The convergence of a power flow is known only from the record that MEME writes next to the network; without it the document says `unknown`.
- A PyPSA network with several investment periods has its costs and emissions counted without the weighting of the periods, and its objective is not reconciled.
- AdOpT-NET0 0.1.10 writes the node design, the operation and the energy balances of the last investment period in place of those of every period; Coati warns about such a file and cannot restore what it lacks.
- Calliope 0.6 needs a version of Python that Coati does not support, so its files are tested from files that were made once; the other frameworks are also solved anew by the tests.
